defender_contentment._comment: How hard a holder can defend their office, by the tribe's average contentment with its 'meter' (Leaders): the holder's rallies against a persuasion campaign and their speeches in an oration are multiplied by this curve [meter, multiplier]. A leader the tribe is fed up with can hardly hold on (x0.2 at 20); a well-liked one defends a little better than usual.

_comment: Ways to take an office other than an election. Each office in data/governments says which it allows, in 'contested_by': {"persuasion": true, "challenge": ["oration", "fight", "skill"]} ('skill' = a skill contest in the challenger's own line of work). Times are hours of the day-night cycle. Meters run 0-100. Power in a contest = the weighted attributes + skill_weight x the skill. 'defender_standing': the office holder's edge in a challenge (0.15 = 15% stronger). Cooldowns: a challenger who loses waits 'cooldown_life_days' day-night cycles before starting another campaign or challenge (a winner doesn't); the holder can't be contested again for 'defender_rest_life_days' (0 = at once: only the loser waits; a new office holder has a grace period instead, time.json 'office_grace_life_days'). 'chosen_by': 'defender' means the one challenged picks the contest (any the office allows; 'skill' = a contest in the defender's own work) within 'answer_life_hours', or the one they are best at is picked for them. 'practice': skill points both contestants gain (win or lose). 'during_contest' says what contestants may still do while a challenge runs; in an audience contest (oration, storytelling) both sides 'speak' to individual listeners (press P), each speech taking 'speak.life_hours' and moving that listener by about 'speak.gain' x their contest strength. 'persuasion.resistance.min'/'max' bound how open a listener can be. 'luck': the role of chance (see its comment).

persuasion.name: Persuasion
persuasion.description: Win the tribe over, one person at a time, until they accept you in the office.

unrest._comment: A campaign starts easier against failing leadership. Each listener starts with extra persuasion of 'per_point' for each point their 'meter' (society.json satisfaction) is below 'neutral'; everyone starts with 'holder_per_point' more for each point the holder's office quality is below 'holder_neutral'. The holder's rally works on a listener in proportion to their meter / 'neutral' (between 'rally_min' and 'rally_max'), and can never push anyone below where they started the campaign. A speech always moves a listener at least 'canvass.min_gain'.

oration.name: Challenge of oration
oration.description: Both speak before the tribe; listeners lean one way or the other.

fight.name: Ritual fight
fight.description: A ritual bout, not to the death: whoever is driven back and yields loses.

hunt.name: Hunting contest
hunt.description: Both go out hunting; whoever brings back the largest animal wins.

gather.name: Gathering contest
gather.description: Both go out gathering; whoever brings back the most food wins.

craft.name: Crafting contest
craft.description: Both make a tool; the finer piece wins.

scout.name: Scouting contest
scout.description: Both range out; whoever returns with the most useful news wins.

lore.name: Storytelling contest
lore.description: Both tell the old stories; the tribe judges who tells them truest.

build.name: Building contest
build.description: Both raise a shelter; the sturdier one wins.

heal.name: Healing contest
heal.description: Both tend the sick; whoever helps more people wins.

during_contest._comment: What the two contestants may do while a challenge runs, by its style. 'locked': they can do nothing else until it ends. 'may': action types, 'care:<kind>' for one care action, and 'speak' (address a listener in an audience contest; the challenger wins them over, the defender pulls them back). Short waits are always allowed.

luck._comment: How much chance there is in contests. Each is a random factor of 1 +/- the value: 'speech' (one canvass, rally or speech to a listener), 'audience' (each moment of an oration, per side), 'duel' (each moment of a fight, per side). 'listener_bias': each listener in an oration starts leaning up to this many points to one side. 'find_size': the range a find is multiplied by in skill contests, for 'best' (largest wins) and 'total' (most wins).
